title: A tool for conflict resolution
metadata: A bilingual dispute-resolution tool with an optional AI-assisted workflow for eligible consumer cases.
intro: Designed for dispute programs, Aequitas organizes evidence and party responses. Optional AI helps prepare non-binding proposals within program rules.
imageCaption: Illustrative image, not a case record.
heroLine: Aequitas can help structure the resolution of disputes and conflicts.
sampleNoticeBody: The people, business and evidence below are invented. This browser simulation does not send or save your choices, call a model, or create a case. Live-model quality and production operations have not been validated. In the app, citations help you find quoted passages in submitted evidence. They do not verify the documents or prove that a passage supports a proposal.

overview.title: Structured dispute resolution
overview.body: Programs use Aequitas to manage two-party disputes through intake, evidence, separate party accounts, proposals, decisions and a recorded outcome.

kind.title: Optional AI assistance
kind.body: For eligible routine retail cases, optional AI can draft an evidence-cited, non-binding proposal. Program rules set eligibility and next steps. AI is off by default.

helps.title: Where it may help
helps.body: Programs may use it to organize recurring consumer disputes, reduce coordination, show support for proposals and flag exceptions. It guarantees no speed or outcome.

inside.title: Rules and software checks
inside.intro: The program defines case types, remedies, deadlines and handoff conditions. Software checks transitions and records actions.

rules.title: 1 · Eligibility and consent
rules.body: Code checks configured eligibility, required submissions and deadlines. Each party separately chooses whether their case information may be sent to the configured AI provider. Without both choices, the service waits or returns the case to staff.

extract.title: 2 · Evidence and citations
extract.body: Supported files are scanned and text is extracted. The system records hashes, extraction details and exact quoted passages for citations. Unreadable, incomplete or unsupported files go to a person; a citation is a navigation aid, not proof.

draft.title: 3 · Proposal checks
draft.body: The model can summarize the record and suggest only from the program’s configured remedy list. Software checks structure, citation links, amount limits and party-specific evidence access. Failed checks or uncertainty stop issuance and trigger staff review.

record.title: 4 · Party decisions
record.body: Parties see their own outcome and choose whether to consent. A decline or request for review goes to staff. Under standard settings, an independent approver must also sign off before closure. The case record can be exported.

limits.title: Aequitas limits
limits.body: Aequitas does not decide who is telling the truth, provide legal advice, verify that documents are authentic, or guarantee that a model’s reasoning is correct or neutral. The current AI workflow has been exercised with synthetic cases and a stub model; live-model quality, real-world operations, program rules, privacy and legal readiness still need validation before real case data. Human review and party consent remain central.

caseDescription: A fictional buyer reports an appliance fault. The shop confirms that a replacement is available. This example uses two short, invented evidence excerpts.

sample.claim: The kettle stopped working after three uses.
sample.response: The shop can replace the item after inspection.
sample.respondentEvidence: Replacement available within 30 days after inspection.

proposalDescription: The app's fixed wording presents the same structured proposal in each person's language.

interaction.title: Compare party views
interaction.description: Switch sides to see how the same fictional case is presented separately. Choose a response for each side to see when the automated service proceeds or stops.
interaction.roleNotice: This browser simulation lets you switch between both fictional roles. In a real case, each party uses a separate account and sees only its own outcome and cited evidence. Staff summaries and reasoning stay private. Responses here are not sent or saved.
interaction.choiceHint: Both parties must consent. Under the standard program rules, a separate approver also signs off before closure.

status.initial: Choose a response for this fictional view. The other party's choice is not shown here.
status.accepted: This view's response is recorded in the simulation. The case stays open until both parties consent and the required approver reviews it.
status.completed: Both fictional parties consented. Under the standard rules, a separate approver still reviews the case before closure.
status.handoff: Automation stops and the case returns to program staff. No agreement is recorded.

intake.title: Intake and invitation
intake.description: Program rules check the case, then the respondent is invited.

evidence.title: Evidence and positions
evidence.description: Each person submits their own evidence and account. Incomplete or unreadable material goes to staff.

proposal.title: Cited proposal
proposal.description: The configured service checks extracted evidence and prepares a non-binding proposal from a closed remedy list.

choice.title: Party choice
choice.description: Both parties may consent. Under the standard rules, the case closes only after their consent and separate approver sign-off. A program can skip sign-off only by explicitly enabling consent-only resolution. Declines, requests for a person and uncertainty return the case to program staff.

handoffBody: Missing, unreadable or disputed material, a case outside program rules, or either person's request stops automation and notifies program staff.

trust.title: Cited proposals and party choice
trust.intro: Aequitas organizes each dispute around party evidence, accounts and choices. Optional AI can prepare a non-binding proposal with citations for eligible cases.

trace.title: Follow the source
trace.body: Citations point back to passages in submitted files, with hashes and extraction details recorded. They aid review; they do not prove a file is authentic or that a quote supports a conclusion.

separation.title: Separate party views
separation.body: Case access rules control who can see submissions and make changes. Each party receives their own outcome and evidence view.

choice.title: Party choice
choice.body: Each party decides whether to consent to the current outcome. Standard program rules keep an independent approver in the closure path.

handoff.title: Human review
handoff.body: A request for review, unreadable evidence, missing information or an out-of-scope case can return work to program staff instead of forcing an automated answer.

trust.readinessBody: The automated case agent is off by default. The demonstrated automated workflow has been exercised with synthetic cases and a stub model. Live-model quality, production operations, program policy and legal/privacy approval still require validation before real cases. Aequitas does not give legal advice.

pilotStatus: The case agent is off by default. This release candidate has been exercised with synthetic cases and a stub model only. It is not approved for real case data.
